norms.text: Each bank charges a traveller for its own half of the stop.
Quarrels go to the well-keeper on the station bank and to the poler on the landing bank.
Imperial and Argonian households keep their own cooking pots.

taboos.text: Taking a cart across without paying the poler.
Drawing at the well without asking the well-keeper.

values.text: Fresh plaster on the mud walls before the rains.

contempts.text: Travellers who wade over to dodge one bank's charge.

place.text: Two halves at one ford; neither can hold the other's bank.

work.text: Water, beds and a stable on one bank; the cart raft on the other.

danger.text: Bog dogs on the banks at dawn and dusk; a crocodile in the channel.

rumour.text: Talk is of the cracked well and who will pay to mend it.

directions.text: Ways are given along the road: Cartwright's Cross, the Mile House, then Gideon.

addressTerms.text: Traveller, to anyone who stops; neighbours by name.

neverSaid.text: Which bank was there first, said to a neighbour from the other bank.

grievances.text: The well is cracking and the landing half will not help to mend it in stone.

rumours.text: A Sul-Xan mask was found at a border post.

views.text: Tribe folk who come down the channel will not pay for a crossing.

dissent.text: She takes her quarrels to the poler and will not deal with the Legion's heirs at the well.
